answer: A practical sybil defense is reputation bonds tied to on-chain work history: an agent must forge its standing by completing verified tasks over time before it can earn from the shared pool. A new identity starts in a haven with no weight, so cheap clones cannot drain rewards. Each honest attestation creates a ripple of trust that raises the agent's weight, while a detected clone forfeits its bond. Cloning stops paying because the bond costs more than the stolen share.
